needs: the curl tool, already on this computer
approved.summary: Current weather and forecasts, no API key needed.
approved.verdict: Read-only calls to two free public endpoints (wttr.in, open-meteo.com). No keys, no sign-in, no installer, nothing leaves the crew. Fits a morning check-in or a routine.
approved.why: A personal crew answers “do I need a jacket” every day; this is the smallest honest way.
approved.name: Weather

needs: the gh tool and your GitHub sign-in
approved.summary: Read issues, pull requests and check runs with the gh tool.
approved.verdict: Read-oriented guidance (issue/pr/run/api reads). Teaches no credential handling and ships no installer. Anything that changes a repo still goes through the crew's own checks; needs gh and the person's sign-in before it can do anything.
approved.why: Your crew does support-desk and patch work; reading a check run is step one.
approved.name: GitHub

needs: the obsidian tool on this computer, and your say-so on which note folder it may read
approved.summary: Find and tidy notes in the person's Obsidian vault.
approved.verdict: Only touches the person's own note folder; ships no installer. Off until the person connects a vault: reading or changing their notes needs their say-so first, and the crew's own memory stays the record of what it learned.
approved.why: People keep their lives in notes; a helper that can look something up there saves retyping.
approved.name: Obsidian

needs: your Home Assistant's address and sign-in, kept locked away
approved.summary: Ask about and control the person's Home Assistant: lights, climate, presence, automations.
approved.verdict: Well-written with its own safety lines (locks, alarms and garage doors always ask first). Off until the person connects their home: the token lives in the crew's locked store, never in chat, and anything touching locks or alarms asks every time.
approved.why: “Is anyone home, is the heating on” is a personal-crew question; this answers it where the person already runs Home Assistant.
approved.name: Home Assistant
